gauntlet.question: What does CPU stand for?
options: Central Processing Unit
Computer Personal Utility
Central Program Upload
Core Power Unit
gauntlet.correct_answer: Central Processing Unit
gauntlet.explanation: The CPU is the main processor that executes instructions in a computer.

gauntlet.question: Which of these is an example of hardware?
options: A web browser
A keyboard
An operating system
A spreadsheet file
gauntlet.correct_answer: A keyboard
gauntlet.explanation: Hardware is physical equipment. Software includes programs, operating systems, and files.

gauntlet.question: What does URL stand for?
options: Universal Routing Link
User Resource Login
Uniform Resource Locator
United Remote Library
gauntlet.correct_answer: Uniform Resource Locator
gauntlet.explanation: A URL is the address used to locate a resource on the web.

gauntlet.question: Which unit is most commonly used to measure file size?
options: Hertz
Bytes
Pixels
Watts
gauntlet.correct_answer: Bytes
gauntlet.explanation: Digital storage and file sizes are measured in bytes and multiples such as kilobytes and megabytes.

gauntlet.question: What is the main purpose of an operating system?
options: To design websites only
To manage hardware and software resources
To replace all application programs
To connect printers without electricity
gauntlet.correct_answer: To manage hardware and software resources
gauntlet.explanation: An operating system coordinates hardware, memory, files, and the programs that run on a device.

gauntlet.question: How is RAM different from a hard drive or SSD?
options: RAM stores data permanently even when power is off
RAM is fast temporary memory used while programs run
RAM is only used to display images
RAM replaces the need for an operating system
gauntlet.correct_answer: RAM is fast temporary memory used while programs run
gauntlet.explanation: RAM is volatile working memory. Drives provide slower long-term storage that persists after shutdown.

gauntlet.question: Why do HTTPS websites use encryption?
options: To make pages load with more advertisements
To hide a site from search engines
To protect data in transit between browser and server
To convert websites into mobile apps
gauntlet.correct_answer: To protect data in transit between browser and server
gauntlet.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS encryption so passwords, cookies, and other data are harder for attackers to intercept.

gauntlet.question: What is the relationship between a bit and a byte?
options: A byte is 8 bits
A bit is 8 bytes
They are two names for the same unit
A byte is 1000 bits
gauntlet.correct_answer: A byte is 8 bits
gauntlet.explanation: A bit is a single 0 or 1. Eight bits grouped together form one byte.

gauntlet.question: What does an IP address identify on a network?
options: The color theme of a website
A device or network interface so data can be routed to it
The brand of a computer's processor
The password used to unlock Wi-Fi
gauntlet.correct_answer: A device or network interface so data can be routed to it
gauntlet.explanation: IP addresses are numeric identifiers used to send packets to the correct host on a network.

gauntlet.question: Why is cloud storage not the same thing as RAM?
options: Cloud storage is always faster than RAM
Cloud storage keeps files on remote servers, while RAM is local working memory
RAM can only store photos
Cloud storage exists only on USB drives
gauntlet.correct_answer: Cloud storage keeps files on remote servers, while RAM is local working memory
gauntlet.explanation: Cloud services store data on remote machines. RAM is short-term memory inside the device you are using.

gauntlet.question: A cafe's public Wi-Fi has no login page. Which practice best reduces the risk of someone reading your traffic?
options: Using HTTP instead of HTTPS for every site
Turning off the device firewall
Using HTTPS or a trusted VPN while on the network
Sharing your screen so others can verify the connection
gauntlet.correct_answer: Using HTTPS or a trusted VPN while on the network
gauntlet.explanation: Open Wi-Fi can be watched by nearby attackers. Encrypted HTTPS or a VPN protects the contents of your traffic.

gauntlet.question: A laptop feels slow while many browser tabs are open, but the disk still has free space. What is the most likely bottleneck?
options: The display resolution is too low
The machine has run out of available RAM
The computer no longer has an IP address
The CPU clock is measured in bytes
gauntlet.correct_answer: The machine has run out of available RAM
gauntlet.explanation: Many tabs consume working memory. When RAM is exhausted, the system swaps to disk and feels sluggish even with free storage.

gauntlet.question: You copy a 5 GB video onto a USB flash drive formatted as FAT32 and the copy fails. What is the most likely reason?
options: FAT32 cannot store a single file larger than 4 GB minus 1 byte
USB drives can only store text files
Videos must be stored in RAM, not on a drive
FAT32 requires an internet connection to save files
gauntlet.correct_answer: FAT32 cannot store a single file larger than 4 GB minus 1 byte
gauntlet.explanation: FAT32 has a maximum file size of 4 GB minus 1 byte, so a 5 GB video cannot be copied unless the drive uses a newer format such as exFAT or NTFS.

gauntlet.question: A phishing email looks like it came from your bank and asks you to 'confirm' a password on a linked page. What should you do?
options: Reply with the password so the bank can verify you
Open the link and enter the password quickly
Avoid the link and sign in only through the bank's official app or typed URL
Forward the email to everyone in your contacts
gauntlet.correct_answer: Avoid the link and sign in only through the bank's official app or typed URL
gauntlet.explanation: Phishing pages imitate real sites. Going through a known official channel avoids handing credentials to an attacker.

gauntlet.question: A team collaborates on a document in the cloud. Two people edit at once and later see unexpected duplicate paragraphs. Which concept best explains this?
options: The CPU has no cache
Concurrent edits can conflict when copies of the same file are changed separately
HTTPS has stopped encrypting the file
The file was converted from bits into watts
gauntlet.correct_answer: Concurrent edits can conflict when copies of the same file are changed separately
gauntlet.explanation: If two users change overlapping content without proper merge or locking, both sets of edits can survive as duplicated or conflicting text.

gauntlet.question: A site loads over HTTPS, but the browser warns that the certificate is issued for a different domain. What is the safest conclusion?
options: Encryption is present, but the identity of the server may not match the site you intended
The page cannot contain any images
Your RAM is full, so certificates cannot be checked
HTTPS warnings always mean the Wi-Fi password is wrong
gauntlet.correct_answer: Encryption is present, but the identity of the server may not match the site you intended
gauntlet.explanation: TLS can still encrypt traffic to the machine you reached. A name mismatch means you may not be talking to the legitimate site.

gauntlet.question: An office computer can open websites by IP address but cannot open them by name such as example.com. Which component is most likely failing?
options: The monitor cable
DNS resolution of domain names to IP addresses
The machine's GPU
The FAT32 file size limit
gauntlet.correct_answer: DNS resolution of domain names to IP addresses
gauntlet.explanation: Reaching a host by numeric IP shows basic network connectivity. Failure by name points to DNS, which translates domains into addresses.

gauntlet.question: A backup copies files every night but is stored on the same disk as the original data. Why is this a weak disaster-recovery plan?
options: Nightly copies use too many IP addresses
A disk failure or ransomware event can destroy both the originals and the backup
Backups are only valid if stored in RAM
Operating systems refuse to read a second copy of a file
gauntlet.correct_answer: A disk failure or ransomware event can destroy both the originals and the backup
gauntlet.explanation: Good backups are separated in location and often offline or versioned, so one incident cannot wipe production data and its only copy.

gauntlet.question: A programmer stores passwords as unsalted SHA-1 hashes. After a database leak, why are users still at high risk?
options: SHA-1 hashes cannot be stored on SSDs
Attackers can try common passwords and compare them to fast, unsalted hashes, especially with rainbow tables
HTTPS will automatically publish the original passwords
The CPU will convert each hash back into the exact original password on boot
gauntlet.correct_answer: Attackers can try common passwords and compare them to fast, unsalted hashes, especially with rainbow tables
gauntlet.explanation: Unsalted fast hashes let attackers test huge password lists efficiently and reuse precomputed tables. Password hashing should be slow and unique per user.

gauntlet.question: Golden Challenge: A traveler uses public Wi-Fi to open a bank site. The browser shows a valid HTTPS padlock, but a rogue hotspot uses DNS spoofing to send the traveler to an attacker server that has its own HTTPS certificate for a look-alike domain the traveler did not notice in the address bar. Which pair of concepts together best explain why the padlock appeared and why the traveler is still in danger?
options: HTTPS can encrypt traffic to whichever host the browser actually connected to, while DNS spoofing can steer the name lookup toward a malicious host if the user does not verify the real domain
RAM encryption makes every Wi-Fi network trustworthy, and FAT32 blocks phishing
The padlock means the CPU verified the bank's private key locally, and DNS is only used for email
Cloud storage certificates replace DNS, so a padlock proves both identity and backup safety
gauntlet.correct_answer: HTTPS can encrypt traffic to whichever host the browser actually connected to, while DNS spoofing can steer the name lookup toward a malicious host if the user does not verify the real domain
gauntlet.explanation: TLS confidentiality is hop-to-the-connected-server, not a guarantee you reached the intended bank. DNS can be abused to land you on a similar-looking domain; the padlock only matches that other certificate. Checking the true URL is the second required defense.
